title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1LC1RD_1LA0RB_1RC1RB_1LF0LC_---0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1LC1RD_1LA0RB_1RC1RB_1LF0LC_---0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. The head sweeps across the whole tape. Most of the tape is one ten-cell word repeated, and the rest, at the right end, is an irregular zone that keeps a roughly constant size of a few hundred cells. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the exact way a halt would happen (A reading 1 with two 0s on its left) and how the head crosses the repeated word; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1011 steps. The whole question is about the irregular zone, which does not repeat.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: How a halt comes about
claims.text: F reading 0 is the only halt. F is entered only from E reading 0, E only from A reading 1, and A only from C reading 0, all moving left (enter_F, enter_E, enter_A). So a halt is exactly 0 E>0, that is 0 0 A>1, that is 0 0 1 C>0.

claims.title: Crossing the repeated word
claims.text: For every n and every surrounding tape, B moving right rewrites (1101101101)^n as (1011110110)^n in 12n steps, and C moving left (in front of 0 0) rewrites (0101111011)^n, a rotation of that, as (0110110111)^n, a rotation of the original word, in 58n steps. So both directions of a sweep cross the run in the same way whatever its length. Other shift rules: B crosses (1 1)^n, D turns (1 0)^n into (0 1)^n, and moving left C turns (0 1 1)^n into (0 0 1)^n and A turns (1 0 1)^n into (1 0 0)^n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator (tools/c/tm.h) runs 1011 steps from blank tape without a halt; the visited tape then spans 202,291 cells, 141,549 of them 1.

claims.title: A never reads 1 next to 0 0
claims.text: In the first 2·109 steps A reads 1 about 229 million times; the two cells on its left are 1 1, 1 0 or 0 1, never 0 0.

claims.title: Z does not repeat for a very long time
claims.text: Because the sweeps cross the run of words in the same way whatever its length, Z can be followed with most copies of the word deleted. This reduced simulation agrees with the full one at all 77,275 visits checked (same K and same length of Z). Run for 7.7·10<sup>8</sup> visits to the left end (about 10<sup>12</sup> steps of the reduced machine, 1.1·10<sup>8</sup> copies of the word), with Brent's cycle check on Z: no repeat, so Z has no cycle of period up to 2·10<sup>8</sup> visits starting in the first 5·10<sup>8</sup>. Z stayed under 500 cells at every sampled visit. That the reduction is exact for all time is not proved: the crossing rules are, the joins at the two ends of the run are not.

claims.title: A long word run and a bounded irregular zone
claims.text: Each time the head reaches a fresh cell at the left end the tape is A>0 (1101101101)^K Z. In the first 3·1010 steps (77,275 such moments) K grew from 0 to 11,055, almost always by exactly one every seven visits (11,002 of 11,056 increases); the first 50 or so cells of Z repeat with the same period of seven visits, feeding the run. The rest of Z is irregular: Z stayed between 269 and 557 cells long and never repeated.

claims.title: Growth shape
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.521). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.388).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The word run is crossed in the same way every sweep, so the question is about the zone Z: whether its evolution (a few hundred cells, irregular, never repeating so far) ever produces 0 0 A>1. If Z were shown to stay bounded and its evolution did not depend on K, Z would eventually repeat, which would prove the machine runs forever; neither is known. Window CTL up to 7 cells and n-gram CPS (widths up to 9, see the README for the larger runs) fail.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine has run 10<sup>11</sup> steps without stopping. Most of its tape is a ten-cell word repeated over and over; at the right end sits an irregular zone of a few hundred cells that keeps changing and has never repeated. This page runs the real machine in your browser and shows the one pattern that would make it stop.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
A reading 1 with two 0s on its left.
B crosses the word run, for any length.
The irregular zone has stayed about this size.

sections.heading: A word run and an irregular zone
html: Stop the simulator each time the head reaches a fresh cell at the left end. The tape is

with K copies of the word and an irregular zone Z on the right. K grows by one copy almost exactly every seven visits to the left end, so the run fills most of the tape (11,055 copies after 3·1010 steps). The first 50 or so cells of Z repeat with the same seven-visit period: that part feeds the run, one word at a time. The rest of Z keeps a size between about 270 and 560 cells, and in 77,275 visits it never came back to an earlier value.

sections.heading: Crossing the word run
html: Moving right, B rewrites every copy of the word in twelve steps, for any number of copies (bword in lean/Rules.lean):

On the way back C turns them into a rotated form of the original word, 58 steps a copy (cback):

0101111011 0101111011 C>0 0   →   C>0 0 0110110111 0110110111   (116 steps)

So every sweep crosses the run the same way, whatever its length, and all the irregular behaviour happens in Z.

sections.heading: The one way to halt
html: The only missing transition is F reading 0. F is entered only from E reading 0, E only from A reading 1, and A only from C reading 0, each step moving left. So the machine stops exactly when
This is proved in Lean (lean/Halt.lean). In 229 million visits the two cells left of A were never both 0.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.521). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.388).
After 109 steps the tape spans 20,564 cells (10,181 left of the start, 4,804 right), with a density of 1s of 0.697.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Bouncer whose tape is a long run of the word 1101101101, growing by one copy every seven sweeps, followed by an irregular zone of 270 to 560 cells that has not repeated; it halts only if A reads 1 with 0 0 on its left.
family: bouncer with a word run and a bounded chaotic zone, word 1101101101
